notes: Company background: programmatic ad personalization platform that must serve creative selection in <80ms p90 to edge servers.
Primary workload: reranking candidate creatives + runtime personalization snippets (mix of short chat-like prompts and embedding lookups).
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 30ms, p90 < 80ms, tail critical for auctions (~1000 reqs/s during peaks).
Cost sensitivity: high — want to minimize per-request token cost during high QPS; interested in optimizer toolkit to estimate unit economics.
Model preferences: prefer open models (Llama2-Chat style family) quantized to 4/8-bit if quality acceptable; open to small curated LLMs for rerank + larger models for complex personalization offline.
Batching/caching interest: strong — want adaptive micro-batching to preserve latency but exploit batch throughput during reconstructable windows; prefix/KV caching for repeated user context.
Quantization interest: evaluate static 8-bit quantization first; need guidance on quality delta vs latency improvements and fallback policies.
Benchmark ask: baseline request — 72h sweep across sequence lengths (30, 128, 512 tokens), concurrency patterns (poisson bursts), and mixed workloads (embeddings + gen).
Routing/fallback needs: route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical requests and fall back to full-precision model if quality fails QA thresholds.
Security ask: SSO/SAML + audit logs + KMS integration; data residency in us-east required for ad-serving compliance; retention controls for ephemeral auction data.
Quote from CTO: 'We can accept minor hallucinations on personalization text but not on scoring — rerank must be consistent and explainable.'
Existing infra: hybrid cloud, uses AWS and GCP — will test dedicated capacity in us-east first then Private VPC for a pilot cluster behind their firewall.
Current POC plan: 1) run hosted API perf baseline, 2) deploy a small dedicated pool with same model/quant profile, 3) measure cost/tokens and tail latency, 4) iterate batch sizes and cache TTLs.
SE notes: need a perf harness (k6 or custom) repo; requested drive link for Redwood perf templates.
Commercial: procurement asked for committed burst pricing and SLA; finance needs an ARR estimate for dedicated commit sizing.
